body:
For info, I have another system with same .vimrc config but different OS that does *not* have the issue:
* Debian stretch 9.0
* Neovim 0.2.0debian1-git20170619123516 (build from source, commit date/time)
* xterm 327-2.

In 0.2.1, check `:help $TERM` and try with the TERM value recommend there for your terminal. xterm-foo is not recommend for gnome terminal.

Thanks for the detailed analysis!

I checked TERM value and tried all suggested values, but to no avail.

I however pushed further because indeed I had some issues to get the truecolors/italics/cursor to work correctly on my laptop. In fact, my minimal .vimrc above was not enough because I forgot to remove my .vim. 

So I searched further the culprit in my .vim/ folder, and it was a `after/syntax/c.vim` plugin. I updated the minimal config above. The setting is the one that sets the highlight for the braces, exactly the one for which underline is enabled.

My guess is that maybe neovim loads the settings asynchronously, and the setting kicks in while displaying the file, and maybe this corrupt the display (this is *wild* *wild* guess ;-) ).
I guess your terminfo file(s) are missing the entry for underline, and the one we have built-in is wrong.

I had some difficulty to reproduce the bug on another laptop (almost identical) with my minimal config + after/syntax files above.

However it helps to pgdn/pgup in the tmp.c file. After some tries, we see that the garbage appears in the middle of the screen.

Regarding terminfo, please note that underline works (they are displayed).

Having a similar issue here. NVIM v0.2.1-944-g77f1392f0 on termite v12-37-g68b92d3 (tried xterm, rxvt, gnome-terminal as well, same problem). No issues when using VIM the the same config.
Minimal config:
```vim
call plug#begin()
Plug 'morhetz/gruvbox'                                                  
call plug#end()
set number
colorscheme gruvbox
````
After resizing the window some characters are displayed in wrong places and statusline tends to jump to the top if resizing is done at the end of file.
From
![https://i.imgur.com/6GoTD2E.png](https://i.imgur.com/6GoTD2E.png)
to
![https://i.imgur.com/xctNkUz.png](https://i.imgur.com/xctNkUz.png)
and from
![https://i.imgur.com/RaePFkd.png](https://i.imgur.com/RaePFkd.png)
to
![https://i.imgur.com/cfi1PcE.png](https://i.imgur.com/cfi1PcE.png)

Issue disappears after removing `set number`

EDIT: NVIM v0.2.0 works fine.

I edited the first post to _minimalize_ further the `.vimrc` to remove all dependency on external plugins. The use of `.vim/after/syntax/c.vim` is now optional (the effect is to change the color of the garbage).

I also added two _screenshots_ of the issue.
This may be related to the "bce" terminal capability. Can you try https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/7624 ?

Update: ef195e8 _always_ disables BCE except for "real xterm". 

Summary:

- Nvim 0.2.0 did not implement BCE. 
- Nvim 0.2.1 enabled BCE aggressively.
- Nvim 0.2.3+ (after this PR) disables BCE (like 0.2.0) in all cases except when the `$XTERM_VERSION` env var is defined.

ref #4210 #4421 #7035 #7337 #7381 #7425 #7618

body:
Hi Justin,
Just tried commit 0b93bab from your fork, but still get similar issue.

I noticed some changes though (from git201710092056+3676, aka v3676). In v3676 and xterm, the garbase message is `[?25l123:131m`, whereas in commit 0b93bab, the message is now only `123:131m`. This is not the only message, but with the new commit, the garbage are always shorter.

I don't see any changes in gnome-terminal though (even when changing TERM).

Also, it is not always easy to reproduce the problem. In fact one should make the test file bigger (like 1280 lines), and press and maintain PgDn, then PgUp keys.

``` bash
for((j=0;j<1280;j++)); do echo "{ $(for((i=0;i<17;i++)); do echo -n '0x00, '; done) }"; done > tmp.c
```

- Terminal name/version: gnome-terminal 3.18.3

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim -u NORC`
No idea. Happens at random, apparently.

### Actual behaviour
Opening up Neovim (using an existing session) sometimes prints the following characters at seemingly random places in the code. This slows down machine considerably. If I scroll past the line with the offending characters, they disappear and Neovim returns to normal responsiveness.

![screenshot from 2017-11-30 10-42-54](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6486383/33424775-201097ca-d5bd-11e7-99ea-8ee87fe54f38.png)

Do not screw up the characters.

![screenshot from 2017-11-30 10-44-27](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6486383/33424785-23928fc0-d5bd-11e7-978d-ee1d48f84407.png)

### Extras
I honestly do not know if this is actually related to Neovim or not, but I thought I'd let you know in case someone had the same issues. I just recently switched to Ubuntu, just as 0.2.2 was released, so I cannot tell you if this was a problem prior to this version.

This is a regression of #3875 which was fixed by #5436.

Possible cause: cdfaecb25f6a9a94f29a38d9f2d24a579b3dff5f , 2c236fc67be2

The buffer length tracking might need a closer look: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/commit/cdfaecb25f6a9a94f29a38d9f2d24a579b3dff5f#diff-3ac88981a139ac0eee448a6bd19c7569R1641

I'm not involved in the development, but I want to help getting this fixed.
This is what I can see:

current HEAD: can reproduce issue
git checkout 2c236fc\~1: can reproduce issue
git checkout cdfaecb\~1: **cannot** reproduce issue

Hope this helps!
